|lore=Extremely common menial-labor droid. Used for a variety of tasks. Mostly used for transporting heavy objects from one place to another.
|game_text=Your vehicles and devices deploy -1 here. Once during each of your control phases, may place your weapon, device or non-creature vehicle present on top of Reserve Deck. When on Crash Site Memorial, that Effect is immune to Alter.

* [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Light Character: ASP-707 (Ayesspee), Special Edition, F
|strategy=By James A. Van Fleet, RED 15<ref name="decipher-strategy">https://web.archive.org/web/20040811081149/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/specialedition/light/small/asp707.html</ref>

The ASP droid is a very nice deploy 1, forfeit 4 character. Why deploy a character with no power or ability? Any card that allows you to take cards out of play and return them to your life Force is a winner! Since characters can carry as many weapons or devices as desired, [[ASP-707 (Ayesspee){{!}}ASP-707]] offers some terrific advantages. Its -1 deploy bonus will allow the Light Side to cheaply deploy duplicate devices from your hand. Then during the control phase, ASP can seed the top of your Reserve deck with a high destiny device or weapon for any upcoming destiny draw.

An extra ASP lost to the [[Crash Site Memorial]] will protect that Effect and help keep weapons, vehicles, and devices recirculating if they are lost from the table. Players can improve on the popular [[Baragwin]] weapon / device retrieval strategy with ASP droids. Baragwins will help negate Dark Side Force drains, even drains

Combo:

[[ASP-707 (Ayesspee){{!}}ASP-707]] + [[Figrin D'an]]. Gamble with confidence! Set up high destiny draws during your control phase, and use them right away.
